overview: In Jain philosophy, 'Dharma-dravya' is one of the six fundamental substances (Dravyas) that constitute the universe. It is distinct from the common understanding of 'dharma' as moral virtue or religious duty. Instead, Dharma-dravya refers to the medium of motion, an essential aspect that allows for the movement of living beings and matter in the cosmos. This concept is crucial in understanding the Jain cosmological framework, where it is paired with 'Adharma-dravya', the medium of rest, to provide a complete explanation of motion and stillness. Dharma-dravya, being non-sentient and infinite, pervades the entire universe and is integral to the function of other substances, notably Jiva (souls) and Pudgala (matter). It is a unique concept that underscores the Jain belief in an ordered and interdependent universe, where motion is facilitated by a distinct substance.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umaswati
primary_sources.translation: There exist (the substances of) Dharma, Adharma, and Akasha.
primary_sources.notes: This text is a key scriptural source for understanding the foundational concepts of Jain metaphysics, including Dharma-dravya.

misconceptions.myth: Dharma-dravya is related to moral or ethical duties.
misconceptions.reality: Dharma-dravya in Jainism is the medium of motion, not related to ethics or morality.
